feedback: Approved to race. The candidate is valid and is a single-variable test against iteration 5, the best raced design (699.16). Geometry is the iteration 5 layout (x ±0.03 m at y 0.06, 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6, wheels unchanged). Only base_speed moves, from 1.2 to 1.1, with kp 2.6, kd 0.9, ki 0.05 and sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] held. Speed is the one lever not yet isolated. Iteration 3 to 4 cut speed and kp together and moved slalom max_error from 0.0646 to 0.0618, while kd and ki alone moved it little (iterations 5 to 7). Iteration 5 finished oval and s-bend 20/20 at 1.2, and the timing margin to the 3 s limit is still comfortable at 1.1. The main risk is a small score loss from longer completion times, not a finish failure. Approving now gives a clean read on speed and is the most useful use of the remaining runs. Read the next race by track. If oval or s-bend finish rate falls below 0.95, or completion_time exceeds about 2.8 s, return base_speed to 1.2. If the slalom still goes off track with max_error at or above 0.06 at 1.1, the controller levers are largely exhausted, so the next structural test is line_loss 'search_right' (or a 3-sensor layout). If any slalom run finishes, hold all values and confirm the score.
requested_changes: If oval or s-bend finish rate drops below 0.95, or s-bend completion_time exceeds about 2.8 s, set base_speed back to 1.2 with kp 2.6, kd 0.9, ki 0.05 (iteration 5: both tracks 20/20, s-bend mean 2.23 s).

If the slalom still ends off track with max_error at or above 0.06 at base_speed 1.1, test line_loss 'search_right' with everything else unchanged. Slalom line-loss events have stayed near 1.0 across iterations 3 to 8, and a different loss response is the untested structural lever.
If any slalom run finishes, hold geometry and controller fixed and use the next race to confirm the score rather than change gains (iteration 5 is the reference at 699.16).
